newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Minority Tamils allege abuses by Sri Lankan army.
newsitem.headline: Minority Tamils allege abuses by Sri Lankan army.

text.p: Sri Lanka's minority Tamil community on Saturday complained of human rights abuses as battles raged between the predominantly Sinhalese forces and Tamil Tiger rebels near a northern guerrilla stronghold.

A pro-government Tamil party urged President Chandrika Kumaratunga to intervene and stop alleged human rights abuses against Tamils and make sure those detained by the army in the Tamil-dominated Jaffna area were tried fairly.
The army, who seized the northernmost Jaffna peninsula in April, is now advancing south towards Kilinochchi, the northern entry point to the Tigers' jungle stronghold of the Wanni.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, fighting for an independent Tamil homeland in the north and east of the country, had ruled Jaffna as a mini-state for almost a decade with their own administration, courts and police.

A military spokesman said the rebels were putting up stiff resistance with heavy rocket-propelled grenade and mortar fire, but the army had resumed slow progress after Thursday's rebel counter-attacks in which hundreds of rebels and soldiers died.
The Defence Ministry said 21 more soldiers were killed on Friday and 46 wounded, while 52 of the 156 wounded in Thursday's rebel attacks had died of injuries in addition to the 75 killed in action.
This raises the army's death toll to 219 and the number of wounded to around 300 since the offensive was launched on Sunday after a lull of more than a month.
A military statement said 35 rebels were killed and 100 wounded, bringing the total Tiger casualties to about 1,500.
The LTTE's daily broadcast did not give a rebel death toll, only saying 196 government soldiers had been killed.
It was not possible to verify the claims as the government has banned journalists from visiting the war zone.

Joseph Pararajasingham, parliamentary leader of the Tamil United Liberation Front (TULF), wrote in the letter to President Chandrika Kumaratunga that 76 Tamils, mostly youths, were harassed by police after being arrested by the army.
"The police have them in their custody for over three months, torture them and obtain confessions under duress," he said in the letter which was made available to journalists.
Pararajasingham said the youths had been taken to Anuradhapura, a Sinhalese-dominated city in the mainland, for trial "though there is a magistrate court functioning in Jaffna".
He said Tamil youths were harassed by a mob that gathered outside a Anuradhapura court. "Anuradhapura is a sensitive area and the safety and security of Tamil youths are in danger," he said.
Two other political parties represented in parliament also complained of human rights abuses in Jaffna.
The LTTE said in its daily radio broadcast that air strikes by the security forces caused many civilian casualties.
"The Sri Lankan ground troops are also carrying out massive shelling day and night on the civilian areas far away from the battlefield," the broadcast said.
It said since the army's pincer offensive on Kilinochchi was launched last Sunday, 27 civilians had been confirmed killed and 50 wounded by air strikes and shelling.
The military spokesman said air strikes were focused on rebel targets.
The LTTE said 50,000 civilians displaced by the current wave of fighting were fleeing to safer areas south of Kilinochchi.
Gerard Peytrignet, representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Sri Lanka, confirmed that many people were seeking safety but was unable to verify the number displaced.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict since it began in 1983.
